title: See where the space went
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

C4: a folder tree the person sees: missing

live-tree-refresh-with-100k-expanded-no-stall: Stand-in tree (none built): refresh median 84 ms (bar 50), UI gap 866 ms (bar 250), scroll jumps

mid-scan-shares-never-exceed-parent: needs first: A read path that gives the tree consistent rolled-up totals for levels 1-4 while the scan runs. Either the scanner thread publishes immutable per-folder snapshots (an extension of TopLev…
Expandable tree versus a flat drill-down list. The FolderSizes page cited describes both shapes. The proposal takes the tree so the path from the drive stays in view.
Files shown as rows next to folders, versus folders only. Row 5's own check opens a folder of 100,000 files, which is why files are rows here.
FolderTreeRowText as its own class versus formatting properties on FolderTreeNode. This is layering, and nothing in the rules depends on it.
A nonzero share that rounds to zero shows '0.0 %' (matches a hand-computed check) versus '<0.1 %' (more honest to the person). The proposal keeps '0.0 %'.
Rows reorder at hand-off from the live flat list (by bytes) to the tree (by on-disk), versus re-sorting the live list by on-disk now. Left alone, since no owed row covers the mid-scan list.

No window case covers the 'could not be read in full' wording for a folder whose listing failed partway (Scanner.cs:158-166). Window cases drive a real scan of a real NTFS tree, and an ordinary user cannot make a directory listing fail partway. The 'could not be opened' branch is covered by B-007's 12 denied folders.

As in attempt 1, the design's Case D re-run of the StallRig network cases (N-001..N-004) was not run. They create and remove SMB client mappings on this machine, which I may not change; they are person-run with -IncludeNetwork.

For SL-039/SL-040's window: moving and resizing the window while a scan starts can block the UI thread for most of a second, depending on the display state. In T-005's shape here, one batch of runs had longest waits of 361–467 ms in the first scan and 378–857 ms in the rescan, and every hand-off peaked at 105–136 ms. Minutes later, the same runs had no wait over 98 ms and moves of at most 28 ms, whether a 100,000-row or a 1-row folder was open before the rescan. The attempt-1 follow-up about the tree's two-row viewport at 880x620 is resolved by O-029 (284 px, 14 rows by default) and can be closed.
